This is called official reserve sale . The decrease (increase) in official reserves is called the overall balance of payments deficit (surplus). The basic premise is that the monetary authorities are the ultimate financiers of any deficit in the balance of payments (or the recipients of any surplus). We note that official reserve transactions are more relevant under a regime of fixed exchange rates than when exchange rates are floating. (See sub heading ‘Fixed Exchange Rates’ under section 6.2.2) Autonomous and Accommodating Transactions International economic transactions are called autonomous when transactions are made due to some reason other than to bridge the gap in the balance of payments, that is, when they are independent of the state of BoP. One reason could be to earn profit. These items are called ‘above the line’ items in the BoP. The balance of payments is said to be in surplus (deficit) if autonomous receipts are greater (less) than autonomous payments. Accommodating transactions (termed ‘below the line’ items), on the other hand, are determined by the gap in the balance of payments, that is, whether there is a deficit or surplus in the balance of payments. In other words, they are determined by the net consequences of the autonomous transactions. During calendar year 2026, a factory had 222 machines on 1 January and 240 machines on 31 December. It added 35 machines and removed 17 machines during the year; these were the only changes to its machine stock. Match each item in List-I with its interpretation in List-II.
List-I
(A) 222 machines on 1 January 2026
(B) 240 machines on 31 December 2026
(C) 35 machines added during 2026
(D) An 18-machine net increase between 1 January and 31 December 2026
List-II
(I) Stock measured at the opening date
(II) Flow measuring additions over the year
(III) Stock measured at the closing date
(IV) Flow measuring the change in stock over the year
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The counts of 222 machines on 1 January and 240 on 31 December are stocks because each is measured at a particular point in time. The 35 additions are a flow over the year, and the net change is 240 − 222 = 18 machines, also a flow because it measures a change over a period. The 35 additions and the 18-machine net increase are different measures.

The distinction between factor cost, basic prices and market prices is based on the distinction between net production taxes (production taxes less production subsidies) and net product taxes (product taxes less product subsidies). Production taxes and subsidies are paid or received in relation to production and are independent of the volume of production such as land revenues, stamp and registration fee. In order to arrive at the market prices, we have to add to the factor cost the total indirect taxes less total subsidies. A firm operating in the short run increases its output from 8 units to 9 units. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) Total variable cost increases.
(B) Total cost increases.
(C) Total fixed cost increases.
(D) The firm can adjust a fixed input to raise output.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only","(A) and (D) only","(A) and (B) only"]
explanation: In the short run, the firm can adjust only variable inputs. Increasing output therefore increases total variable cost, and total cost increases because it is the sum of total variable cost and total fixed cost. Total fixed cost remains fixed, and a fixed input cannot be adjusted in the short run.

(A) The flexible exchange-rate system provides the "float" part, while the fixed-rate system provides the "managed" part.
(B) The arrangement is also called "dirty floating".
(C) Without a formal international agreement, the world has moved to a system best described as managed floating.
(D) The system is a mixture of a flexible exchange-rate system and a fixed-rate system.
Choose the correct sequence:

(See sub heading ‘Fixed Exchange Rates’ under section 6.2.2) Autonomous and Accommodating Transactions International economic transactions are called autonomous when transactions are made due to some reason other than to bridge the gap in the balance of payments, that is, when they are independent of the state of BoP. One reason could be to earn profit. These items are called ‘above the line’ items in the BoP. The balance of payments is said to be in surplus (deficit) if autonomous receipts are greater (less) than autonomous payments. Accommodating transactions (termed ‘below the line’ items), on the other hand, are determined by the gap in the balance of payments, that is, whether there is a deficit or surplus in the balance of payments. In other words, they are determined by the net consequences of the autonomous transactions. Since the official reserve transactions are made to bridge the gap in the BoP, they are seen as the accommodating item in the BoP (all others being autonomous). body: A profit-maximising firm operates in the short run. Its minimum AVC is ₹7 per unit. Its SMC schedule has a descending branch with SMC values ₹16, ₹12 and ₹9 per unit at outputs 1, 2 and 3 units, respectively, and a rising branch with SMC values ₹9, ₹12 and ₹16 per unit at outputs 5, 6 and 7 units, respectively. All listed outputs are feasible, and the firm’s short-run supply curve comprises the rising part of SMC at prices from and above minimum AVC. What outputs does it supply at market prices ₹9, ₹12 and ₹16 per unit, respectively?
options: ["5 units, 6 units and 7 units, respectively.","3 units, 2 units and 1 unit, respectively.","5 units, 2 units and 7 units, respectively.","7 units, 6 units and 5 units, respectively."]
explanation: All three market prices are at least as high as the minimum AVC of ₹7. The firm’s short-run supply curve uses the rising part of SMC, so the relevant schedule points are ₹9 at 5 units, ₹12 at 6 units and ₹16 at 7 units. The descending-branch points do not form part of the stated supply curve.

By how many percentage points did India’s exports to China as a percentage of its imports from China change from 2004–05 to 2024–25?
options: ["It decreased by 84.1 percentage points.","It increased by 669.2 percentage points.","It decreased by 66.5 percentage points.","It increased by 66.5 percentage points."]

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Treatment of imported goods in CPI
(B) Treatment of imported goods in GDP deflator
(C) Weights used in CPI
(D) Weights used in GDP deflator
List-II
(I) Imported goods are excluded
(II) Weights differ according to the production level of each good
(III) Imported goods are included
(IV) Weights are constant
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: CPI includes prices of imported goods consumed by the representative consumer and uses constant weights. The GDP deflator excludes imported goods and uses weights that differ according to each good’s production level. Thus, the correct mapping is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Now suppose the prices of a kg of rice and a piece of cloth has gone up to Rs 15 and Rs 120 in the year 2005. To buy the same quantity of rice and clothes the representative will have to spend Rs 1,350 and Rs 600 respectively (calculated in a similar way as before). Their sum will be, Rs 1,350 + Rs 600 = Rs 1,950. The CPI therefore will be 1,950 1,400 × 100 = 139.29 (approximately). It is worth noting that many commodities have two sets of prices. One is the retail price which the consumer actually pays. The other is the wholesale price, the price at which goods are traded in bulk. These two may differ in value because of the margin kept by traders. Goods which are traded in bulk (such as raw materials or semi-finished goods) are not purchased by ordinary consumers. Like CPI, the index for wholesale prices is called Wholesale Price Index (WPI). In countries like USA it is referred to as Producer Price Index (PPI). Notice CPI (and analogously WPI) may differ from GDP deflator because 1. The goods purchased by consumers do not represent all the goods which are produced in a country. GDP deflator takes into account all such goods and services. 2. CPI includes prices of goods consumed by the representative consumer, hence it includes prices of imported goods. GDP deflator does not include prices of imported goods. 3. The weights are constant in CPI – but they differ according to production level of each good in GDP deflator. 2.5 GDP AND WELFARE Can the GDP of a country be taken as an index of the welfare of the people of that country? If a person has more income he or she can buy more goods and services and his or her material well-being improves. So it may seem reasonable to treat his or her income level as his or her level of well-being. GDP is the sum total of value of goods and services created within the geographical boundary of a country in a particular year. It gets distributed among the people as incomes (except for retained earnings). So we may be tempted to treat higher level of GDP of a country as an index of greater well-being of the people of that country (to account for price changes, we may take the value of real GDP instead of nominal GDP). But there are at least three reasons why this may not be correct. 1. Distribution of GDP – how uniform is it: If the GDP of the country is rising, the welfare may not rise as a consequence. This is because the rise in GDP may be concentrated in the hands of very few individuals or firms. For the rest, the income may in fact have fallen. In such a case the welfare of the entire country cannot be said to have increased. For example, suppose in year 2000, an imaginary country had 100 individuals each earning Rs 10. A case describes a telephone service that remains reserved for the public sector even after private firms are recognised as capable of providing it. Because competition is absent, applicants wait a long time for a connection. Which statements correctly describe the case?

(A) Public-sector reservation can continue even when private firms are capable of providing the service.
(B) The long wait is linked to the absence of competition.
(C) Private firms had already entered and competed when the long wait occurred.
(D) Competition among providers is identified as the cause of the long wait.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

(A) Set out the current and capital accounts as the BoP elements already named in the description.
(B) Note that it is difficult to record all international transactions accurately.

body: At a fixed market price in the long run, four firms supply 80, 60, 40 and 20 units, respectively, before a unit tax. The tax is imposed on the first two firms only. At that price, Firm 1’s supply falls by 20% of its pre-tax supply, and Firm 2’s supply falls by 10% of its pre-tax supply. The supplies of Firms 3 and 4 remain unchanged. What is the percentage decrease in total market supply, measured against its pre-tax level?
explanation: Pre-tax market supply is 80 + 60 + 40 + 20 = 200 units. The reductions are 16 units for Firm 1 and 6 units for Firm 2, so the total reduction is 22 units. Thus, the percentage decrease is (22 ÷ 200) × 100 = 11.0%.

body: A firm operates in the short run. At an output of 20 units, its average variable cost (AVC) is ₹14 per unit. The short-run marginal cost (SMC) of increasing output from 20 to 21 units is ₹11. What follows for AVC when output rises to 21 units?
options: ["AVC must fall below ₹14 per unit.","AVC must rise above ₹14 per unit.","AVC must remain at ₹14 per unit.","The change in AVC cannot be determined from these values."]
explanation: At 20 units, total variable cost is 20 × ₹14 = ₹280. Producing the 21st unit adds ₹11, making total variable cost ₹291; therefore, AVC at 21 units is ₹291 ÷ 21, or approximately ₹13.86 per unit, which is below ₹14.

A colonial official is reported as saying: “India is the pivot of our Empire... If the Empire loses any other part of its Dominion we can survive, but if we lose India, the sun of our Empire will have set.” The statement is attributed to Victor Alexander Vruce, Viceroy of British India in 1894. Match each part of the statement or its attribution in List-I with the interpretation it supports in List-II.

List-I
(A) The official says the Empire could survive the loss of any other part of its Dominion.
(B) The official says that if India were lost, the sun of the Empire would have set.
(C) The official describes India as the “pivot” of the Empire.
(D) The attribution identifies the speaker as Viceroy of British India in 1894.

List-II
(I) Identifies the speaker’s office and the year of the statement
(II) Presents India as central to the Empire
(III) Presents the loss of another dominion as survivable
(IV) Presents the loss of India as the end of the Empire

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The statement says the Empire could survive the loss of another dominion but would end if India were lost. Calling India the “pivot” presents it as central to the Empire, while the attribution gives the speaker’s office and the year.

The structure of India’s present- day economy is not just of current making; it has its roots steeped in history, particularly in the period when India was under British rule which lasted for almost two centuries before India finally won its independence on 15 August 1947. The sole purpose of the British colonial rule in India was to reduce the country to being a raw material supplier for Great Britain’s own rapidly expanding modern industrial base. An understanding of the exploitative nature of this relationship is essential for any assessment of the kind and level of development which the Indian economy has been able to attain over the last seven and half decades. 1.2 1.2 LOW LEVEL OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT UNDER THE COLONIAL RULE India had an independent economy before the advent of the British rule. body:
A rural planning team is identifying water-body types relevant to a fishing community. The team is classifying types, not asserting that fishing takes place at each particular site. Consider the following statements.
(A) A local lake and stream may be included among the water bodies described as an integral, life-giving source.
(B) The description “mother” or “provider” reflects how the fishing community regards the water body.
(C) The water bodies relevant to this description are restricted to seas and oceans.
(D) Rivers and natural aquatic ponds are also among the water bodies named.
Choose the correct answer:
options: ["(A), (B) and (D) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The listed water bodies include lakes, streams, rivers and natural aquatic ponds, and they are described as an integral, life-giving source for the fishing community. The community regards the water body as a “mother” or “provider”. Statement (C) is incorrect because the description is not restricted to seas and oceans.

body: A government records three budget receipts during a period. The first is ₹1,56,000, all of which must be returned. Of the second receipt of ₹2,40,000, exactly 3/8 must be returned. Of the third receipt of ₹1,20,000, exactly 2/3 must be returned. The remaining portions create no liability, and none of the receipts involves the sale or reduction of government assets. What total amount of these receipts is classifiable as capital receipts on the basis of liability creation?
explanation: Receipts that create a liability are capital receipts. The liability-creating amounts are ₹1,56,000 + (3/8 × ₹2,40,000) + (2/3 × ₹1,20,000) = ₹1,56,000 + ₹90,000 + ₹80,000 = ₹3,26,000.

body: A rural-development committee is comparing policy descriptions. It wants to identify the approach that uses the market mechanism to create additional opportunities and links a specific land arrangement to rural social security. Which description correctly combines these relationships?
options: ["Transfer land to individual ownership, allow individuals to cultivate it, and use the market mechanism to create opportunities; link this arrangement to rural social security.","Retain collective land ownership, allow individuals to cultivate it, and use the market mechanism to create opportunities; link the land arrangement to rural social security.","Retain collective land ownership, prevent individuals from cultivating it, and use the market mechanism to create opportunities; link this arrangement to rural social security.","Retain collective land ownership and allow individuals to cultivate it, but attribute the additional opportunities to public intervention rather than the market mechanism; link this arrangement to rural social security."]
explanation: The described approach uses the market mechanism to create additional social and economic opportunities. It links rural social security to retaining collective ownership of land while allowing individuals to cultivate it.

body:
For each case below, consumer income is unchanged. Match each price change with its effect on the slope of the budget line.

List-I
(A) The price of bananas rises while the price of mangoes remains unchanged.
(B) The price of bananas falls while the price of mangoes remains unchanged.
(C) The prices of both bananas and mangoes remain unchanged.
(D) The prices of both bananas and mangoes rise, but their proportional increases are not stated.

List-II
(I) The budget line becomes steeper.
(II) The budget line becomes flatter.
(III) The slope of the budget line remains unchanged.
(IV) The direction of the change in slope cannot be determined from the stated information.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: With the price of mangoes unchanged, a rise in the price of bananas makes the budget line steeper, while a fall makes it flatter. If neither price changes, the price ratio and hence the slope remain unchanged. When both prices rise by unspecified proportions, their price ratio may change in different directions or remain the same, so the direction of the slope change cannot be determined.

body:
In the licensing framework for Indian industries, an existing industrial unit proposes to increase output of its current product without diversifying production. Assume that no exemption from the licensing framework applies. Consider the following statements:
(A) An existing unit could expand output without obtaining a licence.
(B) An existing unit had to obtain a licence to expand output.
(C) An operating licence automatically covered later increases in output.
(D) An output increase required a licence only when it was combined with diversification.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["Statements (A) and (C) only","Statements (A) and (D) only","Statements (B) and (C) only","Statement (B) only"]
explanation: An existing industry had to obtain a licence to expand output, so statement (B) is correct. Since the unit is expanding output, the licence requirement applies even though it is not diversifying production.

body: Under a flexible exchange-rate regime, the initial price of ₹1 is $0.0131. Which later quoted price of ₹1 indicates appreciation of the rupee compared with the initial price?
explanation: The price rises from $0.0131 to $0.0135 per ₹1. Under a flexible exchange-rate regime, an increase in the price of domestic currency (rupees) in foreign currency (dollars) is appreciation. The other listed prices are lower than or equal to the initial price.

body: A district planning panel reports that private schools and clinics are operating alongside public intervention in both sectors. Education and health-care services in the district create both private and social benefits, but many households cannot afford basic access to either service. Expenditure on both services has substantial long-term effects that are not easily reversed. Which recommendation is best supported for the district?

explanation: Both services create private and social benefits, many households cannot afford basic access, and expenditure on these services has substantial long-term effects that are not easily reversed. These stated conditions support public intervention in both sectors, which is already operating in the district.
